{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Corio / Commerce One)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Contract review findings and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is largely acceptable: the Vendor indemnity, audit rights, governing law, renewal mechanics, and the absence of exclusivity, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicit and liquidated damages all sit at or above our preferred positions and require no redline.

Three critical items drive our position. First, § 13.5 contains a proviso that strips our ownership of interface code we create wherever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and our stated walk-away; we have deleted the proviso and can address ongoing support by licence back instead. Second, the liability cap in § 9 is nominally mutual but illusory, being limited to amounts "actually paid" by Corio "for the transaction which the liability relates to", with carve-outs confined to the § 8 IP indemnity; we have reset the basis to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable / USD 1,000,000 and added standard Excluded Claims. Third, the "Corio Market Segment" definition operates as a field-of-use restriction on the customers we may serve, which we have deleted.

Secondary priorities are the licence grant (§ 3), which runs to Corio alone and omits the affiliates and contractors we are expressly permitted to use under § 14.8; the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a five-year committed term (§ 11); assignment consent at absolute discretion with no affiliate carve-out (§ 14); a 60-day warranty period with a fixed 31 December 1999 cut-off (§ 7); and two gaps — no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation (§ 11.3) and no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Finding | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP | § 13.5 proviso transfers Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where it supports them on an ongoing basis; proviso deleted, ownership of the Software under § 2.8 untouched | Deviation | § 13 Shared Resources |
| Critical | LOL-CAP | Cap limited to amounts "actually paid" by Corio for the relevant transaction, no USD 1M floor, carve-outs limited to § 8; reset to greater-of 12 months' fees / USD 1M plus Excluded Claims | Deviation | § 9 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN | Full third-party IP infringement defence and indemnity extending to us and our Customers, standard exclusions and remedies, § 8 liability outside the cap | Compliant | § 8 Indemnification |
| High | NONCOMPETE | "Corio Market Segment" (customers under USD 1bn annual sales) operates as a field-of-use limit, reinforced by the North America Territory; segment limit deleted | Deviation | § 1 Definitions |
| High | LICENSE | Perpetual, irrevocable, M&A-transferable grant, but runs to Corio alone; affiliates and § 14.8 contractors inserted into the hosting grant | Deviation | § 3 Grant of Rights |
| High | T4C | No Customer convenience right in a five-year committed term (§ 11.2 covers only uncured material breach and insolvency); 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees added | Deviation | § 11 Term and Termination |
| High | ASSIGN | M&A carve-out present and no Vendor termination/re-pricing on our change of control, but consent is absolute and there is no affiliate carve-out; reasonableness standard and affiliate right added | Deviation | § 14 Miscellaneous |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | All licences non-exclusive; no sourcing or channel obligation on us; Exhibit D cooperation expressly non-binding; § 2.4 restraint runs in our favour | Compliant | § 3 Grant of Rights |
| High | LD | No liquidated damages, penalties, late interest, shortfall charges or minimum termination payments on us; refunds under §§ 7.3 and 8.1 run in our favour | Compliant | § 17 Payment Terms |
| Medium | WARRANTY | Conformance and no-malicious-code warranties with adequate remedies, but 60-day period from the Effective Date with a 31 December 1999 cut-off; reset to 12 months from delivery | Deviation | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer |
| Medium | TRANSITION | § 11.3 covers survival and return of Confidential Information only; no transition assistance and no data return or certified deletion (escrow in § 12 is not a substitute) | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT | Once yearly, reasonable notice, independent CPA acceptable to us, records-only, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5% | Compliant | § 4 Fees |
| Medium | GOVLAW | California law is on our accepted list; AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County with awards enforceable in California courts | Compliant | § 14 Miscellaneous |
| Medium | MFN | Exhibit B sets fixed pricing and revenue-share percentages with no MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction | Compliant | Revenue Sharing Fees |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | No take-or-pay or shortfall; unlimited Software Users, revenue share only on revenue actually received, Implementation Fees capped time-and-materials; the 40-user reference is an exemption threshold | Compliant | Revenue Sharing Fees |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | No solicitation, hiring, employment or inducement language; §§ 5, 13 and Exhibit D address personnel access only | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources |
| Medium | RENEWAL | 12-month renewals with a 30-day non-renewal window; Exhibit B pre-agrees Year 2–5 and beyond maintenance and MarketSite fees | Compliant | § 11 Term and Termination |
| Low | INSURANCE | No insurance clause in the Agreement or Exhibits despite Vendor personnel working with our hosted environment and MarketSite.net handling our Customers' transaction data; standard CGL, E&O and cyber inserted | Missing | § 14 Miscellaneous |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Assignment of Customer IP — § 13.5.** The proviso transferring Corio-created Developments to Commerce One wherever it provides ongoing support is our walk-away. We have deleted it. Commerce One's ownership of the Software under § 2.8 is unaffected, and its ongoing support interest can be met by a licence back rather than an assignment.

For completeness, the § 9 liability cap is not framed as a walk-away but is a critical deviation we should not concede: as drafted the cap is illusory and confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside it. Governing law and venue (§ 14) are expressly **not** a walk-away case — our preference for courts over arbitration is noted but we would not spend capital there.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and two gaps identified above.
2. **Escalate the three critical items** — § 13.5 IP proviso (delete), § 9 cap (greater-of 12 months' fees paid or payable / USD 1M plus Excluded Claims) and the § 1 market-segment field-of-use limit (delete) — as a linked package.
3. **Hold the fallbacks in reserve:** on the field-of-use point, retain the USD 1bn threshold plus the existing growth/M&A carve-out with a notice-based right to serve larger customers; on IP, a licence back to Commerce One for supported Developments.
4. **Second-tier asks:** extend the hosting grant to affiliates and § 14.8 contractors; add a 30-day Customer convenience right with refund of prepaid fees; add an affiliate assignment carve-out and reasonableness standard on consent; move the warranty to 12 months from delivery and drop the calendar cut-off.
5. **Close the gaps:** insert the transition and data-return clause (six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable export, certified deletion) and the standard insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, certificates on request) in Miscellaneous.
6. **If the deal reopens on indemnities,** add breach-of-law, data-breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs to § 8; otherwise § 8 is acceptable as drafted.
7. **No action required** on exclusivity, liquidated damages, audit, governing law, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicitation or renewal."}
